description: Collaborative weekly meal planner (AWS course final project). Requirements are frozen in docs/requirements.md; architecture is human-owned and partially pending (docs/architecture.md).

rules.requirements_are_frozen: Never edit docs/requirements.md, app_user_stories.md, coverage_analysis.md, gaps_and_resolutions.md or gaps_pending_stakeholders.md. Every R<n> must cite an existing FR-*/NFR-* id.
rules.architecture_is_human_owned: Never decide anything listed in docs/architecture.md section 2. Set status blocked instead.
rules.never_generate_iac_or_ci: Agents never write Terraform, IaC or CI/CD files. init.sh fails if they appear.

tiers.0: Scaffolding. No product requirement behind it.
tiers.1: Pure domain logic. Architecture-independent — buildable and fully testable today.
tiers.2: Ports and application services. Needs the REST contract decided.
tiers.3: Adapters. Blocked on the corresponding architecture decision.
tiers.4: Frontend. Stack decided 2026-08-17 (P7); blocked on the REST contract.
tiers.5: Infrastructure and pipelines. Human-owned, never agent-generated.

features.name: project_scaffold
features.title: Full-stack project scaffold and quality toolchain
features.description: Both toolchain roots. Backend: uv workspace (core + lambda_api + lambda_ai) with pytest, ruff, mypy and pre-commit. Frontend: its own package.json root with React, Vite, Vitest, ESLint and Prettier, the messages and tokens modules, and the es-ES locale constant - bootstrapping a single placeholder component and NO product screens. No product logic either side. Layout per docs/architecture.md section 3.
acceptance: backend/pyproject.toml is a uv workspace root ([tool.uv.workspace] members = core, lambda_api, lambda_ai) with shared ruff/mypy/pytest config
backend/core is distribution planner-core with ZERO runtime dependencies; src-layout package planner_core with domain, application, ports subpackages (each with __init__.py)

backend/lambda_api (planner-api) and backend/lambda_ai (planner-ai) each depend on planner-core only (their AWS/AI deps are added later with their adapters, per P1/P4); src-layout packages planner_api and planner_ai exist
ruff configured (format + check, line length 100) and passing across the workspace
mypy configured in strict mode across the workspace, and passing
pytest configured with the 'aws' marker registered and deselected by default (-m 'not aws'); at least one smoke test passing in core/tests
pre-commit config running ruff format, ruff check and mypy on staged files
uv export --package planner-api --no-dev resolves the api closure without the AI SDK (verifies the split is real)

frontend/ is its own toolchain root with its own package.json (private, ESM), untouched by the Python gates. React and react-dom are its only runtime dependencies; Vite, Vitest, ESLint and Prettier are devDependencies

frontend/src/ and frontend/tests/ exist, with src/messages/ and src/tokens/ as real modules (not placeholders): every user-facing string is UPPER_SNAKE in the messages module and every colour, spacing, font size and breakpoint is a named token (FR-UX-01, FR-UX-03, docs/conventions.md section 'Frontend conventions')
The locale is exported as a constant 'es-ES' used by Intl.DateTimeFormat and Intl.NumberFormat; it is not a runtime setting and no i18n framework is added
package.json declares no CSS framework, no component library, no CSS-in-JS library, no templating engine and no stylesheet - all four are explicit prohibitions in docs/conventions.md

Prettier formats and ESLint lints frontend/ only, both passing, both as devDependencies. ESLint uses flat config (eslint.config.js) with eslint-config-prettier applied last so the two never fight over formatting. Plain JS and ESM with JSX enabled and no TypeScript parser. Chosen by the agent on the human's instruction 2026-08-17 (he does not work in JS and asked for the industry-standard pair); this is the frontend counterpart of ruff

The two toolchains are mutually isolated: the Python gates never read frontend/, the JS gate never reads backend/, and NEITHER reaches prototypes/ (read-only reference material - see prototypes/wireframe/README.md)
pre-commit runs the JS gate on staged frontend files alongside the Python hooks

React is the framework, written idiomatically: function components and hooks, with JSX. Vite is the build tool and dev server, with a minimal index.html entry and a src/main.jsx bootstrap that mounts a single placeholder component - NO product screens, no routing, no API layer (P7, decided by the human 2026-08-17, docs/architecture.md section 1.1)

Vitest is configured as the test runner over frontend/ only, with at least one smoke test passing, asserting behaviour through state and never snapshotting whole views (docs/conventions.md section 'Testing')
Plain JavaScript and ESM throughout - no TypeScript, no tsconfig, no type-checking gate. The frontend has no mypy counterpart by design

./init.sh detects both toolchain roots and runs every gate green, skipping the frontend gate with a WARN while frontend/package.json is absent (same pattern it already uses for backend/pyproject.toml)
No Terraform, no CI workflow, and no runtime dependency on core is added

features.name: week_calendar
features.title: ISO week model and Europe/Madrid scoping
features.description: Current/next live week computation as ISO weeks in Europe/Madrid, plus the today-onward scoping rule shared by AI generation and shopping aggregation. Time enters through a Clock port.
acceptance: A Clock port exists in planner_core.ports; no domain code calls datetime.now()
current_week and next_week are computed as ISO weeks (Monday-Sunday) in Europe/Madrid
A week exposes its 7 days and, per day, the lunch and dinner slots
A week exposes its Monday-Sunday date range for UI labelling (FR-UX-06)
A today-onward scoping function returns only slots from the present day forward for the current week, and all slots for the next week
DST transitions and year boundaries are covered by tests
Tests use a fixed FakeClock; no real clock, no network

features.name: text_and_units
features.title: Fixed unit vocabulary and text normalization
features.description: The shared kernel behind ingredient aggregation: the fixed unit list plus case-, accent- and trim-insensitive normalization.
acceptance: A fixed unit list is defined as a closed vocabulary (concrete values proposed in design.md per G-39)
normalize(name) is case-, accent- and leading/trailing-whitespace-insensitive
Normalization performs no stemming, no singular/plural folding and no synonym matching (G-56 explicitly rejects these)
Tests prove 'Tomate', 'tomate ' and 'tomate' with an accent normalize to one key
A value outside the fixed unit list is rejected with a named domain exception

features.name: recipe_model
features.title: Recipe entity and meal snapshots
features.description: Immutable Recipe with name, ingredients (quantity + unit from the fixed list), tools and procedure; plus the snapshot taken when a recipe enters a week.
acceptance: Recipe is a frozen dataclass carrying name, ingredients, tools, procedure
Recipe carries exactly one tipoAlimento — the predominant ingredient category, from the fixed FR-RULE-04 set (FR-LIB-03, G-69)
Recipe carries no cuisine, difficulty or kcal attribute (G-68, G-36)
Ingredient quantities only accept units from the fixed unit list (FR-LIB-05)
A snapshot function produces a value object decoupled from the library entry (FR-CAND-07)
Test proves editing or deleting the library recipe leaves an existing snapshot unchanged (G-05)

features.name: week_plan_model
features.title: Candidates, definitive selection and attribution
features.description: Slot contents for a live week: add/edit/remove candidates, promote one to definitive, clear the definitive, duplicate warnings, and author attribution with the unknown-user placeholder.
acceptance: A slot holds a list of candidates and at most one definitive (FR-MENU-03)

A candidate is constructible from any of the three authoring sources - a library recipe pick, a from-scratch recipe, or an accepted AI preview - all landing as the same snapshot-backed candidate (FR-CAND-02, FR-CAND-07)
Promoting a candidate replaces any previous definitive; clearing returns all meals to candidate status (FR-CAND-05, FR-CAND-08)
A promoted meal remains editable; edits propagate wherever it is shown (G-67)
Adding a candidate whose normalized name matches one already in the slot returns a warning but still adds it (FR-CAND-01, G-59)
Saving a meal to the library always creates a new entry and warns on same-name collision (FR-CAND-06, G-26)
Every candidate carries its author; promotion records no separate attribution - FR-SUM-02 was removed (FR-CAND-04, G-79)
Attribution resolves to the reserved unknown-user placeholder when the author was removed (FR-SUM-03, G-29)

features.name: rules_model
features.title: Shared generation rules and satisfiability
features.description: The dropdown-only shared rule set: ingredient-category counts, pinned library meals per slot, disabled days; plus the constraint solver that prevents contradictory combinations and the per-run override.
acceptance: The three rule types are modelled: category counts, pinned meal per day/slot, disabled days (FR-RULE-04)
The ingredient-category list is a fixed predefined set (concrete values proposed in design.md per G-63)
Available options are constrained so contradictory rule sets cannot be composed: category totals exceeding available slots after disabled days, or a pin on a disabled day (FR-RULE-07)
Deleting a library recipe referenced by a pin rule surfaces a warning and removes the rule on confirmation (FR-RULE-07, G-20)
A per-run override produces an effective rule set without mutating the shared rules (FR-RULE-05, G-06)
Any user may edit the shared rules; a rule stores NO author - rule attribution was removed from the MVP (FR-RULE-06, G-76, completed by G-78 for FR-RT-02)

features.name: shopping_aggregation
features.title: Deterministic ingredient aggregation
features.description: Pure function from the in-scope definitive meals to the auto-item set. Matches on normalized name + unit, no cross-unit conversion, idempotent by construction.
acceptance: Aggregation derives only from definitive meals; candidates never contribute (FR-SHOP-05, G-04)
Scope is the current week from today onward plus the whole next week (FR-SHOP-05)
Items merge only on matching normalized name + unit; no cross-unit conversion (FR-SHOP-03)
The function is pure and deterministic: same inputs produce the same required-item set, so repeated runs converge (FR-SHOP-10, G-54)
Items carry no provenance: no auto/manual marker, no override state and no record of which week requires them (G-72, G-73)
Test proves running the aggregation twice yields an identical result

features.name: shopping_list_state
features.title: Shopping list state, re-sync and check-off
features.description: The shared list: one flat item shape with no provenance, additive re-sync merge, check-off, and the quantity-changed-while-checked flag.
acceptance: One shared list; an item is a name, quantity, unit and check state, with NO auto/manual marker and no override state (FR-SHOP-01, FR-SHOP-04, G-72)

Re-sync is purely additive: per normalized name + unit it computes the outstanding amount (required minus what checked items already carry) and writes it to the matching unchecked item, adding one if none exists (FR-SHOP-06, G-72, G-77)
Re-sync never removes anything - stale, manual and checked items all survive it (FR-SHOP-04, FR-SHOP-06, G-72)
Test proves two consecutive presses produce an identical list, and that a manual item absent from the computed set is still present afterwards (FR-SHOP-10)
Items are checkable and uncheckable; checked ones sort into a separate section below (FR-SHOP-07, FR-SHOP-08)
Re-sync never writes to a checked item at all - neither its state nor its quantity; no updated-since-checked flag exists (FR-SHOP-08, G-77, supersedes G-44)

Test proves that raising the requirement above what a checked item covers leaves that item untouched and produces a NEW unchecked item carrying the remainder, not the gross amount (FR-SHOP-06, FR-SHOP-08, G-77)
A checked item and an unchecked item may share a normalized name + unit; this is a purchase plus a remainder, not a duplicate (FR-SHOP-10, G-77)
No duplicate-grouping behaviour is implemented - FR-SHOP-11 was removed (G-74)

features.name: password_policy
features.title: NIST 800-63B password policy
features.description: Password validation for the mandatory set-password step: length bounds, no composition rules, no rotation. Breached-password blocklist deferred from MVP (G-83).
acceptance: Minimum length 10, accepted up to at least 64 characters without truncation (FR-AUTH-15)
No mandatory character-composition rules and no forced periodic rotation are enforced (FR-AUTH-15)
Username validation enforces uniqueness among active accounts and reserves the unknown-user placeholder name (FR-AUTH-17, G-42, G-58)
Rejection messages come from the es-ES messages module (FR-UX-03)
features.note: Breached-password blocklist deferred from MVP by G-83 (docs/gaps_and_resolutions.md Part S, 2026-08-26) — owner decision, requirements.md FR-AUTH-15 amended. specs/password_policy/ revised to match (R1-R7) and approved 2026-08-26.

features.name: generation_request
features.title: Generation request, effective rules and idempotency key
features.description: Resolves the effective rule set for a run (shared rules plus optional per-run override), determines target slots, and derives the idempotency key that prevents duplicate candidates and duplicate AI charges.
acceptance: Effective rules = shared rules with the per-run override applied, leaving shared rules untouched (FR-AI-05, FR-RULE-05)
Target slots exclude disabled days; pinned slots resolve to their pinned library meal (FR-AI-11)
Slots already holding a definitive meal are skipped entirely; an existing definitive outranks a pin rule, and the skipped pin is reported rather than applied silently (FR-AI-11, G-71)
Ingredient-category counts describe the week's final state: meals already present count toward each total and generation supplies only the remainder (FR-AI-11, G-71)
For the current week, target slots start at today (Europe/Madrid) — never days already past (FR-AI-11, G-45)
Generation adds candidates and never removes existing candidates or definitives (FR-AI-11, G-18)
An idempotency key is derived from week + slots + effective rules + mode (FR-AI-08; mode added by explicit human decision 2026-08-26, overturning the spec's initial recommendation)
Test proves the same request submitted twice yields one candidate set and one logical invocation
The three modes (library-only / AI-only / mix) are modelled (FR-AI-03)

features.name: ai_prompt_builder
features.title: AI prompt construction
features.description: Provider-agnostic prompt assembly: Castilian Spanish output, configured servings, category counts as explicit instructions, the fixed unit vocabulary, and the healthy/varied-protein instruction.
acceptance: Prompts are assembled as plain data structures with no provider SDK imported (P4 is still pending)
Every prompt states the configured number of servings (FR-AI-13, G-64)
Every prompt instructs Castilian Spanish output (FR-AI-07)
Every prompt instructs healthy, balanced menus that vary protein sources, labelled non-medical (FR-AI-06)
Ingredient-category counts are passed as explicit prompt instructions, and are verifiable after generation against each recipe's stored tipoAlimento (FR-AI-04, G-69, supersedes G-63)
Prompts constrain ingredient units to the fixed unit list (FR-LIB-05, G-48)
Both single-recipe modes are supported: from specifications, and from a library reference plus specifications (FR-AI-01, FR-AI-02)

features.name: ai_output_validation
features.title: AI output validation and preview lifecycle
features.description: Validates model output against the recipe schema and the fixed unit list, and models the accept/discard/regenerate preview plus per-slot failure results.
acceptance: Output failing the recipe schema or using a unit outside the fixed list is rejected, not silently accepted (G-48)
Single-recipe generation produces a preview that can be accepted, discarded or regenerated; nothing persists until accepted (FR-AI-10, G-17)
Each regeneration is a fresh AI invocation consuming the global budget; no per-user quota is counted (FR-AI-10, NFR-AI-01, G-70)
Per-slot results are independent: one slot failing does not abort the others and partial results are kept (FR-AI-09, FR-AI-12)
Insufficient library recipes for library-only or mix mode produces an explicit named failure, never a silent partial result (FR-AI-12, G-66)
Failure messages come from the es-ES messages module (FR-UX-03)

features.name: rollover_job_logic
features.title: Week rollover as an idempotent state transition
features.description: The five-step rollover expressed as a pure, re-runnable transition: archive the ending week, snapshot the shopping list, promote next to current, initialize a new empty next week, clean bought items.
acceptance: The five steps execute in order: archive, shopping-list snapshot, promote next to current, init empty next week, clean bought items (FR-MENU-06, G-61)
The archive snapshot is taken BEFORE the cleanup (FR-ARCH-02, G-53)
The former next week becomes the current week carrying over its candidates and definitives (FR-MENU-06, G-28)
The new next week starts empty; rules never auto-populate it (FR-MENU-06, G-15)
Cleanup removes every CHECKED item unconditionally; all unchecked items are untouched and keep their state (FR-SHOP-09, G-73)
Archived weeks become read-only (FR-ARCH-02)
Test proves re-running after interruption at each of the five steps completes without data loss, double-archiving or double-cleanup (FR-MENU-08, G-61)

features.name: persistence_ports
features.title: Persistence ports and in-memory adapters
features.description: Repository interfaces for accounts, recipes, weeks, rules, the shopping list and the archive, plus in-memory fakes and the contract-test harness that will later run against the real adapter.
acceptance: Ports are typing.Protocol definitions in planner_core.ports with no storage technology leaking into their signatures
In-memory fakes in core/tests/support implement every port and are used by application-layer tests
A contract suite in backend/tests/contract exercises each port and is parametrized to run against any implementation (fake now, real adapter later)
No AWS SDK import anywhere in this feature

features.name: auth_flow
features.title: Authentication, sessions and account lifecycle
features.description: Login, the mandatory set-password step, temporary admin-assigned passwords, stateless session expiry, session invalidation via a revocation marker, admin account management and user removal. No session-tracking persistence and no app-level brute-force lockout - both dropped from the MVP by G-87.
acceptance: Exactly two roles enforced (Admin, User) with strict view separation - admin has no access to meal-planning features, users have no access to the admin view (FR-AUTH-01, FR-AUTH-05, FR-AUTH-06)
Authentication is username + password only; no self-registration; accounts are created only by an admin (FR-AUTH-02, FR-AUTH-03)
Neither role may change its own password except through the mandatory set-password step (FR-AUTH-04)

Exactly one admin account is provisioned via IaC bootstrap at deploy time; multiple admins are supported thereafter; admin accounts are never created, provisioned or removed through the application (FR-AUTH-07, FR-AUTH-18)
Admin recovery is by IaC re-seed of the bootstrap admin's secret, landing at the same mandatory set-password step as any other temporary password (FR-AUTH-08)
Authenticated sessions and logout are enforced; no session table or per-request persistence - authentication is stateless, a token carries user_id and issued_at (FR-AUTH-09, G-87)
A first login and every admin-issued password (creation, change, reset) is temporary and forces the set-password step before granting access - it never admits directly (FR-AUTH-10, FR-AUTH-11)

An admin password reset or a user removal invalidates every active session of the affected account via a revocation-marker attribute on the account record, checked against the token's issued_at - no session table, no per-session delete (FR-AUTH-11, FR-AUTH-14, G-87)

The revocation marker is written on the same update a password reset already makes to the account record; user removal needs no separate invalidation write - deleting the account record already fails every lookup for its tokens (FR-AUTH-11, FR-AUTH-14, G-87)
The admin view lists every account (username, role, pending set-password status) and launches reset/rename/removal from that list (FR-AUTH-12)
Removing a user retains and reattributes their authored content to the reserved 'unknown user' placeholder rather than deleting it or blocking removal (FR-AUTH-13)
Password policy is enforced via the existing domain module (password_policy.py, feature 9) - no re-implementation (FR-AUTH-15)
Sessions expire after a flat 30-day lifetime from issuance, computed from the token alone with no database access; no inactivity-based expiry (FR-AUTH-16, amended by G-87)
Usernames are unique among active accounts; a removed account's username may be reused; the 'unknown user' placeholder name is reserved and renders as a distinct system label (FR-AUTH-17)
NFR-SEC-04 (login brute-force protection) is NOT implemented here - it moves to infrastructure (feature 21, G-87); no failed-attempt counter, no lockout state, no per-login-attempt write

No external identity provider is introduced - credentials and the revocation marker are owned and persisted by the application via the AccountRepository port (feature 14), per docs/architecture.md section 1.2.3

features.name: rest_api_lambda
features.title: REST API Lambda - HTTP shell and event boundary
features.description: The api Lambda's transport layer: routing, request parsing and camelCase serialization, domain-exception to RFC 9457 error mapping, the REQUEST cookie authorizer, ETag/Cache-Control emission, the SQS producer call site and the EventBridge rollover entry point. Split from the original whole-feature spec on 2026-08-31 (GQ4, owner): the DynamoDB adapters, the planner_core application use cases and the RuleRepository port change are feature 27 rest_api_persistence_and_services.
acceptance: Implements the contract in docs/rest_api_contract.md (decided 2026-08-30, architecture.md section 1.2.5): /v1 base path, English camelCase JSON, RFC 9457 application/problem+json errors with a machine-readable code extension member and detail copied verbatim from planner_core.messages, 400 malformed vs 422 domain-rejected

Every access pattern in docs/rest_api_contract.md section 2 is routed to exactly one method + path template, plus the computed GET /v1/live-weeks; AP3, AP9, AP29 and week rollover have no route; no GET route writes through a repository port

The four pollable resources (weeks, library, shopping list, rules) emit ETag = marcaCambio as a strong validator on 200, mutations echo the marker their write returned, and Cache-Control: no-store is set on every response. If-None-Match parsing, the marker-first read and the 304 mapping are feature 26 realtime_channel_transport (GQ2, owner 2026-08-31)

Auth via a REQUEST-type Lambda authorizer reading the HttpOnly session cookie, authorizer result cache TTL 0, userId/role/passwordResetRequired passed in authorizer context; the handler gates role and passwordResetRequired from that context without a second AP2 read (docs/rest_api_contract.md section 5)

PUT/DELETE /v1/rules/{ruleId} route to feature 27's single-rule operations (AP23/AP24) and UnsatisfiableRuleSet maps to 422 UNSATISFIABLE_RULE_SET with details.conflicts; the whole-set satisfiability check itself is feature 27
GET /v1/weeks/{weekId}?include=ingredients (AP9) is NOT exposed publicly (docs/rest_api_contract.md section 7 Q13)

A non-HTTP entry point for scheduled week rollover (EventBridge Scheduler, docs/rest_api_contract.md section 7 Q8) lives in this package, not a third Lambda, and leaves identical persisted state on re-invocation. Archive is parked for the MVP (owner 2026-08-31, docs/data_model.md section 9 parks FR-ARCH-02 with no item type): wiring.py injects a no-op ArchiveRepository that retains nothing and logs the discarded ArchivedWeek through the standard-library logging module. The real adapter and the snapshot item type are post-MVP
The api package never ships the Bedrock SDK; the api to ai hop is an SQS enqueue through the GenerationQueue port (architecture.md section 1.2)
Structured logging through the standard-library logging module on every invocation; no print; no traceback or stack frame in any response body (NFR-OBS-01)

The session cookie is HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Path=/; Max-Age=2592000, the token never appears in a response body, and DELETE /v1/session expires the cookie on the same response that advances validoDesde

SCOPE: the DynamoDB adapters, the GenerationQueue SQS adapter, the new planner_core application use cases and the RuleRepository save_rule/delete_rule change are feature 27 rest_api_persistence_and_services, which this feature depends on

features.name: ai_lambda
features.title: AI generation Lambda
features.description: The ai Lambda: provider client, per-slot concurrency, idempotent invocation, cost cap enforcement.
acceptance: Provider client targets AWS Bedrock + OpenAI GPT-5.6 Terra (architecture.md section 1.2.6, model changed 2026-09-16 from the original Anthropic Claude choice - owner lacks Bedrock model-access permissions for Anthropic models): global.openai.gpt-5.6-terra via Bedrock's Converse API (this model has no InvokeModel support on bedrock-runtime), plain boto3, no new dependency; the model id is env-overridable (AI_MODEL_ID); the Bedrock SDK path is this package's dependency only, never api's
Consumes from the api to ai SQS queue (architecture.md section 1.2); the HTTP surface is submit-then-poll per docs/rest_api_contract.md

Cost cap is a REAL kill-switch (G-81 resolved 2026-08-30, not alert-only). Decide the mechanism in this spec: reserved concurrency 0, event-source-mapping disable, or a flag the worker reads before invoking Bedrock. Global cap, no per-user counter (NFR-AI-01, G-70)

Idempotency: idPeticionIA is a deterministic hash of the request including a server-authoritative attempt ordinal (count of completed generations for the slot, never a client click counter) so a double-submit dedupes; the server also returns 409 for a slot that already has a pending/running generation (FR-AI-09 per-slot concurrency). See docs/rest_api_contract.md section 7 Q3

CONSTRAINT (recorded 2026-08-27, G-88): whole-week AI generation must write candidates through the same WeekRepository port every other write path uses (save_slot/save_week per feature 14/18), never a separate write path - MarcaCambio's marker bump lives inside that port's methods (docs/data_model.md section 4.7), so any write that bypasses the port silently produces candidates other clients' polling never detects.

features.name: realtime_channel_persistence
features.title: Real-time change markers — persistence and ports
features.description: The data-layer half of real-time support (G-88, architecture P3, split from the original realtime_channel 2026-08-27): the MarcaCambio item type (one per pollable partition - weeks, library, shopping list, rules), the current_version read and version-returning writes on WeekRepository/RuleRepository/ShoppingListRepository/RecipeRepository, and their contract tests. No HTTP layer, no handler, no polling logic - that is feature 26, blocked on P5.
acceptance: A MarcaCambio item type exists, one instance per pollable partition (SEMANA#<idSemana>, BIBLIOTECA#<idBiblioteca>, COMPRA#<idLista>, GRUPOREGLAS#<idGrupoReglas>), per docs/data_model.md section 1

WeekRepository, RuleRepository, ShoppingListRepository and RecipeRepository each gain a current_version read (AP29 shape, docs/data_model.md section 4.7) — a cheap, strongly-consistent read of only the marker

Every mutating method on those four ports returns the resource's new version instead of None, and bumps marcaCambio inside the same atomic operation as the data write it marks — never a separate call, never before the data write (docs/data_model.md section 1.1/5.5)

The marker is never used as a write precondition/ConditionExpression on any port method — mechanically enforced by a scan test, mirroring test_ports_are_storage_agnostic.py's technique (docs/data_model.md section 1.1's explicit warning)
Fakes (FakeWeekRepository, FakeRuleRepository, FakeShoppingListRepository, FakeRecipeRepository) implement the version bump with a simple in-memory counter

Contract suites assert: every mutating method changes the version; no read method changes it; the version a write returns equals what the next current_version() call reports; delete_checked_items() with nothing checked stays a no-op and does not bump (its existing idempotency guarantee, feature 8, is preserved)
No handler.py, no wiring.py, no HTTP concern of any kind — this is pure planner_core (domain/ports/application) plus contract tests, the same shape persistence_ports (feature 14) already established

A bulk logical operation (whole-week AI generation, shopping-list re-sync) bumping its marker once per underlying item write, rather than once for the whole operation, is accepted as correct-but-not-optimal for this feature — collapsing it to one bump is explicitly out of scope here (docs/data_model.md section 4.2/4.4)

features.name: archive_and_cold_storage
features.title: Archive browsing and cold-storage lifecycle
features.description: Reverse-chronological archive navigation, indefinite retention, and the scheduled job moving records older than ~3 months to cold storage with a restoring state in the UI.
acceptance: Deferred until the datastore and cold-storage wiring are chosen
features.blocked_reason: PARKED, MVP scope (docs/data_model.md section 9) — not an open decision. Cold storage (FR-ARCH-03) and the reverse-chronological archive browse (FR-ARCH-04) both stay out of the MVP; reaffirmed by the owner 2026-08-30 when P6 was decided. FR-ARCH-04 is not free: idSemana is in the partition key, which DynamoDB cannot list or sort. Unpark needs an explicit owner decision.

features.name: frontend_spa
features.title: Single-page application
features.description: The responsive es-ES SPA: two live weeks, candidates and the three-way authoring flow (library pick / from scratch / AI, reused by library authoring minus the self-pick), definitive selection, library, rules, shopping list, summary and archive. A Claude Design prototype exists at prototypes/wireframe/ (analysed in docs/frontend_prototype.md) — an executable wireframe to mine for colour tokens, es-ES strings, screen inventory and handler names, NOT portable code; see docs/frontend_prototype.md section 4 for the eleven places it contradicts the frozen requirements.
acceptance: Idiomatic React (function components, hooks, JSX), Vite, Vitest, ESLint + Prettier, plain JS/ESM (architecture.md section 1.1); custom hook owns state/handlers/API calls, component is a pure function of props; inline style objects off a shared tokens module (docs/conventions.md 'Frontend conventions')

acceptance: Recipe and MealSnapshot carry an optional servings count and an optional estimated prep/cook time (FR-LIB-03)
Both fields are freeform — no validation, no dropdown constraint, no format enforcement
Both fields can be set in every recipe-authoring flow, manually or by AI generation, with no cross-recipe consistency requirement (FR-AI-13, G-85)
Neither field is read by shopping-list aggregation or any other domain logic — proven by a mechanical scan, mirroring test_no_ambient_time.py's technique (G-85)
The detail-view content model includes both fields alongside ingredients, tools and procedure (FR-MENU-04)
AI output validation accepts the fields as optional and freeform, with no new failure mode when either is absent
The AI prompt builder's CONFIGURED_SERVINGS deployment-config constant (feature 11) is removed; no code path still treats servings as global config

features.name: realtime_channel_transport
features.title: Real-time collaboration channel — transport
features.description: The HTTP-facing half of real-time support (G-88, architecture P3, split from the original realtime_channel 2026-08-27): the api Lambda's conditional-GET handling (If-None-Match parsing, 304 mapping), and the frontend's adaptive polling hook, backoff, connection-loss indication and optimistic self-updates. Also owns the shopping-list re-sync marker-bump collapse (docs/data_model.md section 4.4 note / section 5.3): making re-sync its own transaction instead of a loop of AP19 calls so COMPRA#<idLista>'s marcaCambio bumps once per re-sync rather than once per differing item — the single bump added at section 5.3's lock release. Depends on feature 18's persistence half and feature 16's REST contract.
acceptance: api Lambda conditional-GET handler: parse If-None-Match, do the cheap strongly-consistent marcaCambio read first, return 304 (ETag echo, no body) on match else 200 with the payload and new ETag (docs/rest_api_contract.md section 6)

Frontend adaptive polling hook: per-resource interval, backoff on tab hidden/blurred, immediate resume on visibilitychange, capped jittered backoff on repeated failures; N consecutive failures surface connection loss; optimistic self-updates keep a mutation's returned marker only when it equals held + 1, else refetch (FR-RT-01/-02/-03)

Shopping-list re-sync bumps COMPRA#<idLista> marcaCambio once per re-sync, not once per differing item — re-sync becomes its own transaction, single bump at docs/data_model.md section 5.3's lock release

features.name: rest_api_persistence_and_services
features.title: REST API persistence adapters and application services
features.description: The substrate the api Lambda shell calls, split out of feature 16 on 2026-08-31 (GQ4, owner): the real DynamoDB adapters for every api-side port, the GenerationQueue port and its SQS adapter, the new planner_core application use cases (week/library/shopping/rule editing and generation submission), and the RuleRepository per-rule port change docs/rest_api_contract.md section 7 Q5 requires. No handler, no routing, no HTTP concern - feature 16 owns those and depends on this.
acceptance: A DynamoDB-backed implementation of AccountRepository, WeekRepository, RecipeRepository, RuleRepository and ShoppingListRepository lives under planner_api/adapters/dynamo/, using the partition key, sort key and Spanish attribute names docs/data_model.md section 1 and section 3 assign; no Spanish attribute name reaches planner_core, and planner_core imports no boto3 (architecture.md section 3.1 rule 3)

The real adapters pass the existing per-port contract suites in backend/tests/contract/ unchanged, alongside the in-memory fakes (architecture.md section 3.2); moto-backed, running in the default gate

Every mutating adapter method bumps marcaCambio inside the same TransactWriteItems as the data write and returns the resulting value; no ConditionExpression ever references marcaCambio; current_version is a strongly-consistent marker-only read (docs/data_model.md section 1.1/4.7/5.5)

GQ3, resolved 2026-08-31: RuleRepository gains save_rule(rule) -> int and delete_rule(ruleId) -> int and loses save(RuleSet); rule ids are deterministic natural keys (cat#<category>, pin#<day>#<slot>, day#<day>); DisabledDay becomes a frozen value object in domain/rules.py so a disabled day is individually addressable (docs/rest_api_contract.md section 7 Q5, docs/data_model.md section 4.5)

rule_editing validates whole-set satisfiability in memory before committing the single-item write; an unsatisfiable result raises UnsatisfiableRuleSet and performs no write. library_editing implements the section 3.4 pin cascade: an unconfirmed delete reports the affected pins, a confirmed delete removes recipe and pins (FR-RULE-07)

The shopping-list re-sync composition reads the week in-process (AP9, never a public route), is purely additive, never modifies a checked item, and is serialized by the FR-SHOP-10 lock (docs/rest_api_contract.md section 3.3, section 7 Q13). Collapsing its marker bumps to one per re-sync stays feature 26's acceptance item 3

A GenerationQueue port in planner_core.ports names no queue technology; its SQS adapter lives in planner_api/adapters/; generation_submission derives idPeticionIA via domain/generation and returns a stored result (AP26) without enqueuing (FR-AI-08)

The new use cases live in planner_core/application/ and take only ports and plain values - no HTTP, event or AWS type in any signature (architecture.md section 3.1 rule 2, conventions.md thin-handler rule)

features.name: single_recipe_generation
features.title: Single-recipe AI generation submit-then-poll path
features.description: The end-to-end submit path for single-recipe AI generation (FR-AI-01/-02), the piece feature 12 (ai_output_validation) explicitly deferred to a later feature: the POST /v1/generations single-recipe request body, the server-authoritative attempt ordinal folded into idPeticionIA so an FR-AI-10 regenerate gets past FR-AI-08 idempotency (rest_api_contract.md section 7 Q3), and the ai Lambda branch that builds the prompt (feature 11), invokes the provider under the cost gate (feature 17), runs validate_and_preview (feature 12) and writes the preview into the PETICIONIA# result via GenerationQueue write-back - never through WeekRepository, since a single-recipe result persists nothing until the user saves it as a candidate or library recipe (rest_api_contract.md section 3.1). Split out on 2026-09-06 rather than widening feature 17 (owner). Needs a contract-doc lift: section 3.5 / section 7 today document only the type:"week" body. Owner ruling 2026-09-13: also owns completing the frontend AI authoring-tab, which feature 20 ships only as a disabled stub (spec-input fields, es-ES 'not available yet' notice) pending this feature's contract.
acceptance: OWNER-OWNED PRECURSOR: rest_api_contract.md gains the single-recipe POST /v1/generations request body (discriminated - ingredients + tools per FR-AI-01, or a reference library recipeId plus extra specifications per FR-AI-02; carrying the target day/slot) and the attempt derivation, added the way section 7's gate rulings were. The spec_author proposes the shape at the spec gate; the owner edits the contract before implementation begins

attempt is server-authoritative (rest_api_contract.md section 7 Q3): the count of COMPLETED generations for the target slot, never a client field, folded into idPeticionIA so a retry dedupes and a regenerate misses, and two fast clicks compute the same value (FR-AI-08, FR-AI-10)
domain/generation.py (or a sibling module) gains a single-recipe request type and an idempotency key that includes attempt; the existing whole-week key is untouched

The ai Lambda gains a single-recipe branch: prompt build (feature 11 build_specification_prompt / build_reference_prompt), provider invocation and cost gate (feature 17), validate_and_preview (feature 12), then write estado / resultado onto the PETICIONIA# item via the GenerationQueue write-back method - no WeekRepository call, no MarcaCambio bump
GET /v1/generations/{id} returns the single-recipe preview in result and DELETE discards it - both already built in feature 16; this feature adds no route handler beyond the _submit_generation branch

Per-slot concurrency for single-recipe (FR-AI-09): a submit for a slot that already holds a pending / running single-recipe generation follows feature 17's resolution of its own per-slot-concurrency gate question (a per-slot marker item type, or exact-hash-resubmit dedupe only)

Frontend: replaces feature 20's disabled AI-tab stub with the real submit + poll UI (spec-input form for from-scratch, reference-recipe picker for library-based, wired to this feature's POST /v1/generations body and GET /v1/generations/{id} polling) - React/Vite, no business logic in the client, per architecture.md section 1.1

features.name: rules_dropdown_constraints_wiring
features.title: Wire FR-RULE-07's preventive dropdown constraints through the API and SPA
features.description: FR-RULE-07's preventive half ("dropdown options shall prevent contradictory combinations") is claimed by feature 6 rules_model's acceptance, but feature 6 is tier 1 (pure domain) - it built the constraint functions (max_selectable_count, available_days_for_pin, available_days_to_disable in backend/core/src/planner_core/domain/rules.py) without ever wiring them to an HTTP response or a dropdown. Today the SPA's RulesView (feature 20) renders every fixed-value option always and relies solely on the reactive 422 UNSATISFIABLE_RULE_SET (feature 27) - the requirement's preventive behaviour is undelivered end-to-end despite feature 6 being done. Found during feature 20's final review (2026-09-14); not a defect in feature 20, which correctly scoped only the reactive route.
acceptance: OWNER-OWNED PRECURSOR: rest_api_contract.md needs a shape for exposing the available/constrained option sets per rule type - e.g. GET /v1/rules gaining an availableOptions field (max selectable count per category, days still available to pin, days still available to disable), computed via rules.py's already-built pure functions. The spec_author proposes the shape at the spec gate; the owner edits the contract before implementation begins

Backend: routing.py's _list_rules (or a new field on the same response) computes and returns the available option sets using the existing pure functions - no new domain logic, this feature only wires it through the API

Frontend: RulesView's add/edit dropdowns (category-count select, pin-day select, disable-day select) render only the options the API reports as available, replacing today's full fixed-value lists - the constraint is enforced by not offering the option, never by client-side validation logic (architecture.md section 1.1)

The existing whole-set 422 UNSATISFIABLE_RULE_SET check (feature 27) is untouched and stays the last line of defense for a race between two concurrent edits; this feature only narrows what a single well-behaved client can submit

features.name: library_delete_pin_cascade_ui
features.title: Frontend warning + retry for deleting a library recipe pinned by a rule
features.description: rest_api_contract.md section 3.4's two-step pin-cascade delete (DELETE /v1/library/recipes/{id} -> 409 PIN_RULES_AFFECTED with the affected pins, confirmed retry with ?confirmCascade=true -> 204) is fully implemented server-side (library_editing.py, feature 27) but has no frontend consumer. Feature 20 frontend_spa's useLibrary.remove sends a plain DELETE and surfaces any rejection as generic error.detail text (R15's convention) - a real pin-rules-affected conflict shows the backend's raw problem+json detail with no way to proceed, instead of the warn-then-confirm flow FR-RULE-07 (G-20) describes. Found during feature 20's final review (2026-09-14); flagged rather than fixed there since it needed its own scoped task, not a silent addition to a closing feature.
acceptance: Backend already implements the full two-step cascade (rest_api_contract.md section 3.4, feature 27) - this feature adds no backend code

Frontend: useLibrary's remove handler (feature 20) catches a 409 PIN_RULES_AFFECTED ApiError specifically, shows the affected pins (day/slot) in a confirmation dialog reusing useConfirm.js/ConfirmDialog.jsx, and on confirmation retries the same DELETE with ?confirmCascade=true
No client-side business logic beyond assembling the retry URL and rendering the affected-pins list - the recipe/rule deletion decision itself stays server-side (architecture.md section 1.1)

Test: a 409 response opens the cascade-warning dialog with the correct day/slot text; confirming re-issues DELETE with confirmCascade=true and the item disappears from both the library and rules views; cancelling leaves the recipe and its pin rule untouched
